Params: Thousands of feet below the fireworks, in a place beyond the reach of cheers and clamor...

Below the luminous city, the vast form of the structure takes shape, wrought from moon rock and alloy. It houses the Transatlantic Economic Community's most prestigious research and engineering facilities.
Every current of energy and every stream of data that courses through the ocean converges here, flowing toward its deepest chamber, the heart of all things, the Sefirah Engine.

A machine reminiscent of a Stygiomedusa gigantea hovers within the vast chamber, its tentacles pulsing at a steady rhythm. On the central platform, Arius Erhorn is surrounded by glowing displays, his attention fixed on the formless points of light drifting inside the cubic experimental pod before him.
Quiet footsteps approach from behind, but he does not turn.
The silver-haired man with a mild demeanor steps forward and places one of the two mugs he carries onto the console's edge, the pale amber liquid swaying gently inside.
Not even a sip? I grabbed it from the counter on the way down.
He lifts his own mug and takes a sip.
Did the radiation on the moon finally get to you? Made you forget that neither of us has ever bothered with holidays?
Play whatever game you like, but you know that doesn't work on me.
You haven't set foot in the Atlantic Eye in a year. You came here to ask me something.
Dominik offers no denial. His thumb traces the edge of his mug, and his eyes drift to the dim light pulsing at the heart of the Sefirah Engine.
I've seen next year's plan, the one the Transatlantic Great Family Council is announcing tomorrow.
You're a co-founder of the Atlantic Eye. You have access.

The TEC is cutting civil and environmental projects across the board. Desalination, ecological restoration, trans-oceanic public transit routes... Over 30% of the budget is gone. Labs are being shut down and repurposed.

And in their place, the planetary transformation project is being pushed into geologically unstable deep-sea zones. And based on the projected energy output from simulations, the Sefirah Engine's processing capacity will be pushed beyond its original limits.
You're walking a line that's dangerously thin.
I'm walking the path we set together.
The hooded man turns his head, his tone as offhand as if he were remarking on the weather.

Use the energy from the planetary transformation project to process the highest-density information—the Sefirot—from the collective unconscious system known as the Consciousness Tide. That is the means to resist the Filtering.
That is the only purpose of the Phylotree of Ousia under all that pretense.
Its branches reach across the world, but only one of them bears fruit this quickly.

"Understanding", the Sefirah that defines the structure of all things through reason, capable of simulating a M.I.N.D. and even a miniature Consciousness Tide. We believe it is the key that can help us decipher all other Sefirot.
As a scientist, are you really going to blame me for real progress?
As a scientist, you should know better than to twist the argument and deflect the question.

The Consciousness Tide has peaks, just like the human mind does. Pushing the processing output beyond its threshold is like cutting an unplanned opening into the dam. And if that opening runs out of control, if the peaks break through...
Our single point in spacetime will never hold energy on that scale. Instead of receding, it will only fill the only room we have until it breaks. And that is very—
Adjectives are always relative. They change depending on what nouns they attach to.
We take the "dangerous" road because the "end" waiting for humanity is a thousand times worse.
And you know that better than me. Otherwise, you wouldn't have moved Project Eden up ahead of schedule.

The Army Hiring Act is a well-played move. It takes someone who knows the Transatlantic Economic Community intimately to wield its resources so effectively. The families use Trillard as a pawn, but he clearly sees a more far-reaching opportunity in you.
A go-between of that caliber isn't easy to come by. Someone must have arranged the introduction. The Norman family, or maybe Kowloong?
I don't have your way with words. Just tell me what you're getting at.
I squeeze everything I can from the planet and the TEC. You mobilize the World Government's strength.
Admit it, our approaches are not that different.
This plan touches too many areas. Even if a small circle agrees behind closed doors, once it's announced, there will be resistance.
But there's nothing that can't be done. The only question is whether you're willing to pay the price to make it happen.
He calls up another holographic display and pushes it toward Dominik.
You have people planning your moves. So do I. When it comes to maneuvering against our own, humans have accumulated more wisdom than any field of natural science can claim.
A long silence fills the space, with only the low drone of the Sefirah Engine to break the stillness.
Dominik closes his eyes and exhales a long, heavy breath.
Arius has turned back to his work, but his hand stops mid-motion, and a trace of disbelief flickers across his face.
That's the real reason you came here.
What did you see? What do you know? Why?
Because we see so little and know so little, but we're capable of so much.
As if finally allowing exhaustion to catch up with him, he looks at his own reflection in the mug and offers a bitter smile.
The plan is moving too quickly. Human ability has already surpassed what we predicted. The more we stake on it, the more it will slip beyond our control.
The happiness of individuals and the fate of entire populations should never be taken lightly. But we do, just because they're in our way.
We're burning the "present's" chance to breathe and adapt for a future we're trying to force into shape.
Arius cuts in, barely holding back his irritation.
You think the plan is running away from you because you've let people without the foresight, the backbone, or the strength carry it.
Chase too far and you waste what you have, like the planners of this celebration. See too little and you go nowhere, like the businessmen who look at M.I.N.D. technology and see only coin.
The masses are mediocre, through and through.
They believe whatever suits them, or cling to what they already hold. They're fuel waiting for a flame, still water waiting for a wind.
He braces his lean frame against the console and lifts his chin.
But you and I are the hand that holds the torch, the wind that creates waves.
Fire that doesn't spread burns out. Wind that doesn't move dies down.
Arius, if there's no room for "people" in our plan, then even if humanity passes the Filtering, where does it go from there? And if it doesn't, what's left of it?
Whether humanity passes it or not, the new world is waiting.
A sharp, unnameable fire burns in his eyes as he finally picks up the mug set aside and lifts it toward the man who once stood with him to create miracles.
Only that is worth celebrating, by any measure.
Dominik regards him with a distant, faraway look.
Then he lifts his own mug and taps it gently against Arius'.
They each sip from their cups, and a long silence falls between them.
I'll start my own course next year and teach the kids in the Watcher program about the Consciousness Tide.
The tides are already turning. No one can hold them back now, not even you.
Dominik gives no reply and walks toward the sealed hatch.
The door slides open, then shut. Silence returns to the chamber.
In the dim light, the Science Council's inaugural Chief Research Officer retrieves his terminal and calls up a pale golden interface.

A phantom string of light shoots from the terminal, stretching forward like a guiding thread. The silver-haired man follows its trace, his figure swallowed by the intricate network of corridors surrounding the Sefirah Engine.
His destination is not marked on any structural chart of the dam. It moves constantly beneath the Atlantic Eye, its very existence and the algorithms that dictate its path kept under strict seal.
Beyond multiple layers of access restrictions lies a small, concealed room, its walls covered floor to ceiling with precision instruments. It resembles the interior of a classical mechanical clock.
Dominik inputs the updated Sefirah analysis values into the central processing model.
Initialize with these parameters and run the "dam break" projection.

Projection initiating. Day 0: Analysis output surpasses critical threshold. "Understanding" Sefirah structural integrity is compromised. Consciousness Tide energy is discharged from the Sefirah Engine.
Day 1: Surges breach the surface. Physical order collapses across all sectors of the Atlantic Eye. All personnel suffer consciousness dissolution. Survivors: zero.
Day 9: Energy propagates through ocean currents and atmospheric systems. Transatlantic Economic Community coastal settlements go dark sequentially. Consciousness dissolution spreads inland.
Day 41: Global communications and governance infrastructure collapse. Day 83: Human consciousness retention rate: 0.4%. Irreversible.
Day 84: All civilizational activity ceases. Projection ends.
The hidden chamber is so silent that the faint tick of the precision instruments is audible. Dominik tweaks the parameters and enters them again.
Pre-set early warning protocols. Cut the engine power supply. Mobilize all global energy reserves as a counterweight. Resume projection.
Detonate the dam. Use the Atlantic Ocean as a buffer zone. Continue.
He tries variable after variable, scheme after scheme. The date of ruin moves forward, then back, yet the final outcome remains unchanged.
...Isolate the common factor across all failure outcomes.
"Peak energy load exceeds the maximum capacity for absorption and dissipation within this spacetime."
Within a single spacetime, all interventions can only delay the event but never prevent it.
He straightens slowly. Ytterbium-174 surfaces from the depths of his memory. That strange particle's decay rate slows as its energy increases, and its spacetime properties have never been verified.
Revise premise: Assume a carrier channel using Ytterbium-174 rays, capable of shunting energy to other spacetime coordinates and distributing the peaks evenly across enough spacetime nodes.
Projection complete. Residual energy within this spacetime remains below the cataclysm threshold.
The tension finally leaves Dominik's body. He exhales a long, slow breath.
If one spacetime can't bear the weight, then it doesn't have to bear it alone.
Use this projection as the baseline and update Ananke's full specifications. Scale up channel count, dispersal capacity, and activation threshold, all to match the new runaway scale.
The blueprints unfold across the display. This safeguard, constructed in secrecy from the Atlantic Eye's very first day, now starts to take on a new form—
A sprawling grid of spillways opens outward, channels leading to countless spacetime points.
Calculate the theoretical peak energy reading of Ananke rays and cross-reference it with Reading 0 from the Helio estate.
He stands at the console, stiff and silent, like a man awaiting his sentence.
Conclusion: equivalent. All previous runs of this query yield the same result.
The current, incomplete Ananke cannot emit radiation at that level. Which means the mysterious individual carrying Reading 0...
You're from a future where the worst has already happened, where Ananke has already been set in motion.
What did you come here for?
In your future... did any of what we fought for...
Dominik buries the unspoken words. His fingers clench, release, and come to rest, poised and steady above the console.
No matter what, we have to be ready.
I hope the day you need it doesn't come too soon.
The Next Evening\nChief Risk Control Officer's Office, Helio Headquarters
A knock sounds at the door, precisely on time.
Adelyde pushes the door open and finds the office dark.
The tall woman leans back in her chair, head resting on one hand, casually spinning a throwing knife between her fingers. Her bio-enhanced jade eyes glow faintly in the dimness.
A subtle scent of blood reaches the girl's nose.
(She's obsessive about hygiene. She'd never walk around smelling like her prey's blood. That means...)
You're hurt? You're not patched up properly?
The family head sent an urgent summons. I may have been a bit rushed.
Nothing to worry about. Pain keeps the mind clear.
In the blink of an eye, Adelyde is already in front of her, holding the medical kit that is always kept in the office.
...You really need to do something about that stubbornness of yours.
Even so, Rusalka unfastens her collar and silently allows her student to inspect her shoulder.
The blood didn't soak through, at least.

She works with practiced efficiency, sanitizing her hands and opening a fresh dressing. She peels away the bloodied bandage with a gentle touch and cleans the reopened wound carefully, just as she has done every time she has tended to Rusalka before.

Energy and infrastructure are industries as geopolitically tangled as they are prone to conflict. Anything requiring the Helio Chief Risk Control Officer's personal intervention always carries hidden dangers beneath the surface.
The woman's exposed human skin is layered with scars, none removed or hidden. And the rest of her body...
Adelyde presses her lips together, finishes the bandaging in silence, and waits until Rusalka has redressed before she finally speaks.
Yeah. Better performance and easier maintenance.
Though no matter how many times you bring it up, I won't approve modifications for you, not yet. You take that shortcut before your style's fully set, and you'll break yourself.
The girl, who is indeed deeply fascinated by mechanical prosthetics, quietly edges a small step backward.
It's just... they look different from the designs you usually use.

This bionic spinal-scapular unit came from the Erhorn family as a gift. Stability still has room for improvement, but in strength and sensitivity, it outdoes Copperfield, and they've been in this business for generations.
Adelyde's eyes flicker at the words. Rusalka notices the change and lifts an eyebrow.
Given trial cycles and sample constraints, prosthetics and bionics aren't a field where breakthroughs come easily.
Precisely. The Erhorn family was just the front. The real manufacturer is Kurono, and they recently went public with their majority stake in Erhorn.
They've been moving fast in tech lately. But they're also no strangers to grey-zone experiment scandals. And every time, they just walk away clean...
A queasy sensation twists in her stomach. Adelyde's thoughts spin, the answer lodged in her throat, and then she catches the nod from Rusalka.
The Erhorn-Kurono alliance must have been in place long before the official announcement.
They're investing in their biggest rival instead of deepening ties inside the TEC. Why?
Who knows. I think someone's looking to shake things up.
And that's exactly what I wanted to see you about.
She stands and places a hand on the black velvet box that has been waiting on the desk.
Adelyde steps forward and lifts the lid.
Rusalka chuckles softly at the sight of those wide red eyes and gives her a gentle push toward the lounge.
Go put it on. Let me see for myself.
A moment later, a figure dressed in white emerges from the lounge.
The tailored uniform frames the girl's upright posture, gold threads tracing the collar and sleeves, a sapphire-blue sash crossing her shoulder.
On her left chest, the crest of a seahorse carrying the sun gleams bright.
Like a blade pulled from its scabbard, Adelyde suddenly sheds a veil of childishness and stands startlingly sharp.
The official investiture is still a way off, but you've already earned the right to wear the family colors on official duty.
Rusalka, the Helios' Cruising Vanguard, sets her palm on the shoulder of her student and the future family head, guiding her to face the mirror.
They are dressed identically, the same crest on their chests, though their faces are not the same. But the fire in their gazes matches. She leans in, her voice a low murmur beside Adelyde's ear.
The storm is coming. Some will run. Others step into the eye.
I know you're close to the Copperfield-sponsored student. And to the Spelmin heiress. But when the table is turned, you need to be clear about what you're fighting for.
She cannot find the words. Suddenly, the family crest she once dreamed of wearing feels heavy and scorching hot against her chest.
